title: Platform safety controls show a gap between user action and confidence that the platform will respond
source_unit: Nationally representative UK adult survey of platform safety-technology awareness, use, and satisfaction; published 2026
geography: United Kingdom social-media users; comparative digital-culture evidence, not a US population estimate

observations.period: Data collected January 2023; 1,067 usable UK adult responses; published 2026

denominator.unit: usable UK adult survey responses after removing respondents reporting no daily social-media use

harm_witnessed.unit: percent reporting they had witnessed harmful online content

harm_directly_received.unit: percent reporting they had directly received harmful online content

unfollow_use_among_aware.unit: percent who had used the feature among those aware

block_use_among_aware.unit: percent who had used the feature among those aware

report_use_among_aware.unit: approximately percent who had used the feature among those aware

always_satisfied_block_or_unfollow.unit: percent reporting always satisfied with outcome

always_satisfied_report.unit: percent reporting always satisfied with outcome

satisfied_feed_controls.unit: percent satisfied with altering/deactivating feed or hiding engagements

observations.method: Peer-reviewed survey separating awareness, self-reported use, and satisfaction for seven user-facing safety technologies; the study used a nationally representative UK adult design and logistic models for predictors of use.
observations.uncertainty: The survey is UK-based, collected in 2023, and measures self-reported use and satisfaction rather than platform logs, independently verified harm reduction, wellbeing, or durable exit. Tool availability varies by platform and satisfaction is outcome-specific.
observations.subgroup: UK adults who use social media; analyses also examine harm concern, prior exposure, digital literacy, gender, political orientation, age, and education.
observations.counterinterpretation: High use of blocking or unfollowing can represent active control, repeated exposure, or the burden of self-protection; low satisfaction with reporting may reflect platform responsiveness, severe harms, or mismatched expectations rather than the absence of any benefit.

boundary: This record adds a user-action and perceived-outcome stage to the platform/data lane: awareness, safety-tool use, and satisfaction are separated. It is comparative UK evidence and does not establish US prevalence, causal harm reduction, platform responsibility, mental-health improvement, or durable account exit.
